_what: The district geometry for every surface that draws Proarc's marks: the menu overlay's constellation (09-menu §6), Home's map beat and /ajman's standing map (05-ajman §2). One source, so the three cannot disagree.
_counts: There are no counts in this file, deliberately. A district's mark count is DERIVED from data/projects.json by build/lib/districts.js, so a resolved O5 duplicate or a landed district changes the output and never the design (09-menu §6). Today that derivation yields 28 marks across the ten districts below.
_positions: PLACEHOLDER, and labelled as such wherever it renders. E7.1 splits the map into three layers and the commission supplies only one — coastline and boundaries. The marks are the page's, at true pixels. Until that artwork lands these cluster centres carry the constellation (Option B), which is a constellation and not cartography: it claims relative grouping, never a coordinate. Centres are carried unchanged from board 16 rev 2, which Mahesh saw and approved. When the commission lands, replace `centre` per district and nothing else.
_marks: E7.2 — no mark is placed by inference. A record earns a mark only if its own location string names a district. The 18 plain-Ajman records and the one Umm Al Quwain record have no mark until their data does; they are not approximated onto the drawing.

coast._what: A ROUGH shoreline, drawn in house on Mahesh's instruction (4 Aug 2026) so the client has something to react to. NOT sourced, NOT surveyed, and not the commission's artwork. It is to be fine-tuned or replaced once ProArc approves the shape.
coast._why_a_rough_one_is_safe_where_a_TRUE_on: Session VIII refused to draw a real coastline, and the reason was never that a coast is hard to get — it is that a REAL coast under PLACEHOLDER cluster centres turns every one of those centres into a coordinate claim, and the page becomes more wrong for being more real. A rough coast does not do that: it is invented, the marks are invented, and the two are honest about each other. This is board 12's own footer applied consistently — 'map geometry is invented and labelled as such'. If this line is ever replaced with sourced geometry, the ten `centre` values have to land in the same pass, and ODbL attribution becomes due at that moment.
coast._shape: The Gulf lies north-west, so the shore runs roughly north-east to south-west down the left of the field with the city inland of it. Placed against the MARKS as built, never against the authored centres — jitter moves a mark up to 30 units off its centre, so the centres are not where the drawing actually is. Al Zorah sitting closest is correct rather than tight: it is the coastal development.
coast._clearances: Re-measured 4 Aug 2026, after scatter.minSeparation moved every mark. THE SHORE IS NOW A CONSTRAINT ON THE SCATTER, not just a line the scatter was fitted around: build/lib/districts.js clears every mark of this path by the same minSeparation it clears marks of each other, so these numbers are now MAINTAINED rather than achieved once. That change caught its own need — the separation rule alone had pushed Al Zorah's cluster to 7.1 units off the water, and a mark's radius is 8.75 units at the narrowest band, so the dot would have crossed the line it was being measured against. Marks: Al Zorah 23.6, Al Khor 31.2, Marina & Creek 68.4, everything else past 150. Labels, which sit 26 units below their cluster and run about 52 wide: Al Khor 21.7, Marina & Creek 53.4, Al Zorah 63.6. The labels are NOT constrained in code — they are derived in build/lib/ajman.js from the marks, so they move when the marks do and this line is the record of where they landed. Re-measure it when the path is fine-tuned.
coast._deliberately_absent: No creek and no Emirate outline. The creek cannot be routed between the Al Khor and Marina & Creek labels without running through one of them — the corridor between them is about 18 units and a stroke plus clearance does not fit — and OSM carries no named waterway for it to be checked against. An Emirate outline is a BOUNDARY, and §3.2 is explicit that an invented boundary looks exactly like a real one to whoever is judging it. Both wait for the fine-tune pass, and both are cheaper once the client has reacted to the shape.

scatter._what: How a district's n records are spread around its centre. Deterministic — a seeded generator, never Math.random() — so a rebuild is byte-stable and a diff means the data moved.
scatter._minSeparation: TWO MARKS ARE TWO BUILDINGS, so they have to be countable (Mahesh, 4 Aug 2026 — three pairs in Al Jurf had merged into single blobs, the closest 3.2 units apart). This is the floor on the distance between ANY two marks, across districts as well as within one, and it is in USER UNITS while the fault it prevents is in SCREEN pixels: the mark is a true 5px at every width (E7.1), so the drawing scales under it and the ≤639 band renders a unit at 320/560 = 0.571px. A 10px dot therefore needs 10 ÷ 0.571 = 17.5 units just to stop overlapping there, and 17.5 is a knife-edge of the kind the coast dash already taught this file to distrust. 20 buys a 1.6px gap at the narrowest band and 7.3px at desktop. It is NOT raised further: at 24 a label anchor lands 9.2 units from another district's mark and the names start belonging to the wrong dots, which is a worse fault than a tight gap. Measured, not guessed — the table is in the 4 Aug session record.
scatter._whyNotABiggerMap: Because no width fixes 3.2 units. Ten screen pixels of clearance at that separation needs the field drawn 1,770px wide. The overlap was in the generator, not in the size.
